topic_tag: an early modern agreement between port cities
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
blank_sentence: Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.

worlds.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. Each city's envoys drafted a preamble listing the other's seizures of its ships, and diplomats of the period routinely struck such lists from final texts. Both lists survive in the signed copy, beside a closing clause in which each council says it doubts the other will keep the terms; the dozen fee rules between them took two years to settle and were still being collected in the 1790s. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
worlds.explanation: The signed text kept both lists of grievances that diplomats normally deleted and admitted mutual doubt, so it was above all "candid." "Expedient" fails because its terms took two years to settle and lasted seventy years. "Ceremonial" fails because its fees were actually collected, and "exhaustive" fails because it held only a dozen fee rules.

expedient.why: A slowly negotiated, long-lasting settlement was not a quick measure for a passing need.

ceremonial.why: Fees actually collected mean the agreement had practical force.

exhaustive.why: A dozen rules cannot cover every case.

worlds.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. A fever closed one city's port that year, leaving its grain ships nowhere to unload before the harvest spoiled. Its envoys drafted it in two days, and the signed copy's two clauses let those ships dock across the bay, free of any fee, until the port reopened; its preamble praises the cities' "ancient brotherhood," a phrase both councils' letters treat as a joke, and harbor logs show the arrangement lapsing after some forty ships had used it. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
worlds.explanation: Drafted in two days to rescue one harvest and allowed to lapse once the port reopened, the agreement was above all "expedient." "Candid" fails because both councils privately joked about its talk of brotherhood. "Ceremonial" fails because forty ships used it, and "exhaustive" fails because it dealt only with those grain ships until the port reopened.

candid.why: Public words both sides privately mocked are not frank.

ceremonial.quote: after some forty ships had used it
ceremonial.why: The agreement had real practical use.

exhaustive.quote: let those ships dock across the bay
exhaustive.why: It addressed one emergency, not every case.

worlds.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. It was signed at a three-day feast after a procession of both councils through each city, and its text consists of pledges of friendship with no fees, schedules, or penalties. Harbor logs for the following decade show the same tolls charged, the same ships turned away, and the same seizures of each other's vessels as in the decade before. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
worlds.explanation: A feast and procession produced pledges that changed nothing in the harbors, so the agreement was above all "ceremonial." "Candid" fails because its pledges of friendship sat beside continuing seizures. "Expedient" fails because it met no practical need, since nothing changed, and "exhaustive" fails because it set no rules at all.

candid.quote: the same seizures of each other's vessels
candid.why: Pledging friendship while seizures went on is not frank.

expedient.quote: the same tolls charged, the same ships turned away
expedient.why: An agreement that altered nothing served no practical purpose of the moment.

exhaustive.why: A text with no rules covers nothing.

worlds.passage: In 1724 two rival port cities signed an agreement on the use of each other's harbors. Its envoys spent four years on it, and the signed copy runs to three hundred clauses, from the fee for a barrel of salt to the handling of a ship driven by storm into the wrong harbor; earlier drafts show each case added after a merchant from one city or the other had raised it. Its wording follows the courtly formulas of the age throughout, and harbor logs show joint courts enforcing its terms for a century. Having compared the surviving drafts, one historian judged the final agreement to be above all ______.
worlds.explanation: Four years of drafting added clause after clause until three hundred covered even storm-driven ships, so the agreement was above all "exhaustive." "Candid" fails because its wording follows courtly formulas rather than plain speech. "Expedient" fails because it took four years and lasted a century, and "ceremonial" fails because courts enforced it.

candid.quote: follows the courtly formulas of the age
candid.why: Conventional diplomatic phrasing is the opposite of frankness.

expedient.why: A slow, thorough settlement is not a convenient quick fix.

ceremonial.quote: joint courts enforcing its terms for a century
ceremonial.why: An enforced agreement was not merely for show.
